biography: Anthony Beltoise, a name once synonymous with raw speed and audacious overtaking, hails from the sun-drenched Riviera, a heritage he wears as proudly as his racing overalls. The son of a former rally driver, Anthony's infatuation with speed began early, tearing around go-kart tracks before he could even reach the pedals of a street car. His breakthrough came at the French GT Championship, where his aggressive driving style and uncanny ability to extract every last ounce of performance from his machinery earned him a coveted spot with Chevrolet. A defining moment arrived at Spa-Francorchamps, where, despite a damaged suspension, he wrestled his car to a podium finish, showcasing his tenacity. Now, at 36, while flashes of brilliance still ignite the track, consistency has become a challenge. The young guns are snapping at his heels, and the sparkle of his early career has begun to dim, forcing Beltoise to contemplate his legacy in the sport.
drivingStyle: Beltoise is a driver who lives on the ragged edge. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks in corners, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. While this aggressive style can yield spectacular results, it also leads to inconsistencies and the occasional costly mistake. Tire management is not his forte; he favors short bursts of intense speed over long-run conservation, making him a formidable opponent in sprint races but vulnerable in endurance events. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest.

famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, even if it means bending the rules a little."
careerHighlight: Winning the French GT Championship in 2012, a dominant performance that cemented his status as one of the country's most promising young talents.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while leading, costing his team a likely victory and severely damaging his reputation.
